Ben / Marissa —

Quick initial triage (pulled from the artifacts Sophie sent):
- The edge trace shows several HTTP/1.1 chunked requests that include trailing headers (metadata) after the final 0-length chunk. Our streaming parser currently assumes trailers are rare and treats a trailer frame as an error when it arrives interleaved with multiplexed body frames from the upstream CDN.
- When the parser hits an unexpected trailer, it emits a parse error and tears down the connection. For Warm connections we see the app reconnect storm that raises p99 and drives saturation.
- Repro rate with their traffic shape is ~1-2% of requests but concentrated in checkout bursts which is why BrightMart notices it during peak.

Short-term mitigation options (ranked):
1) Route BrightMart's traffic to a non-multiplexing ingress path (no streaming multiplex) — lowest risk, immediate, requires config flip and maybe capacity adjustment.
2) Server-side coalescing on their CDN (suppress trailing headers) — requires ops on BrightMart side, moderate effort.
3) Fast patch to parser to accept trailers interleaved with body frames (we have a prototype fix, but needs canary).

I’d recommend option (1) while we push a canary for (3). I can prepare a canary patch (patch-825.diff) and a targeted deploy to route their account to the canary.

I’ll start the canary prep and coordinate with infra. Lauren: flagging because this has exec visibility on the customer side and renewals are involved.

— Jonas
